title: Toasts done right.
summary: This reel teaches five essential rules for designing toast notifications: optimal positioning, severity-based timing, stacking limits, user-controlled dismissibility, and accessible color coding. It emphasizes creating non-intrusive, informative UI elements that respect user workflow.

transcript.text: Most toasts break three of these five rules.
Rule 1: Position. Desktop toasts live bottom-right. Mobile goes top. Never center. Center blocks what users are actually doing.
Rule 2: Timing. Info dismisses at 4 seconds. Warnings hold 7. Errors stay until the user acknowledges. A fixed timer is a bug.
Rule 3: Stacking. Maximum three visible. New ones push old ones up with spring physics. Damping 20, stiffness 180. Anything else feels cheap.
Rule 4: Always dismissible. A close button, swipe on mobile, pause on hover. If users can't escape your toast, it's not a toast, it's a modal.
Rule 5: Color coding. Each type needs an icon plus a left border color. Background tint alone isn't enough. 6% of users can't distinguish it.
Five rules. Zero excuses. Follow for more design details. Save this for your next toast implementation.

on_screen_text: 6% of users can't tell them apart
before_after: Contrasts centered toasts (which block content) with corner or top-aligned toasts that remain non-intrusive.
